notes: Trigger cases only. Every skill in the claude/workflow group is installed for
every case, because a group is the unit people install -- so a case can fail by
the wrong sibling firing, not just by silence.
The should_not_trigger arm is mostly other members of this group. These skills
are adjacent by design (plan/execute/delegate, request/receive review), so the
queries that discriminate between them are the ones worth measuring. Obvious
non-matches would report a precision none of them has earned.
should_trigger: The feature is done and all tests pass. Should I merge, open a PR, or something else?
Implementation is complete. What's the right way to integrate this work?
I've finished this branch. Walk me through wrapping it up.
Work's done and green. How do I land it?
This branch is ready. What are my options for getting it into main?
Everything passes. Help me decide how to finish this off.
The task is complete -- what's the cleanest way to close it out?
Done implementing. Time to integrate; what should I do?
should_not_trigger: Review my changes before I merge them.
Remove the worktrees I've finished with and delete their branches.
Merge main into my branch and fix the conflicts.
Write a plan for the next feature.
The tests are still failing. Keep going until they pass.
Set up a new Python package.
